# Independent audit: component affine normalization and the integral lift

**Result: PASS.** I independently checked
`candidate 6ce49e79dcaf76f1`,
its connected-example dependency, and its dependence-component and
universal-graph dependency. I reran

    work/math-venv/bin/python supporting computation verify_integral_connected_universal_lift.py

The exact verifier passes. No mathematical correction is required.

## 1. The criterion has the necessary connected scope

Section 1 explicitly fixes a CONNECTED dependence component. Under
that hypothesis, L(P)=Aff(P) is both necessary and sufficient for
uniform common continuous normalization and ordinary affine-shear
position control. The initial reduction of a component to its
intrinsic saturated affine lattice is legitimate: its convex hull
contains no additional ambient integer points, and a saturated
integer basis identifies those points with a standard lower-rank
lattice. Sections 3--5 about the integral graph do not require
connectedness, and correctly apply to arbitrary full-rank finite
lattice-convex P.

Connectedness cannot simply be removed from the normalization
criterion. For instance P={0,1} has L(P)=Aff(P), but in continuous
dimension two the independent endpoint rectangles

    A_t=[-t,t] times [-1/t,1/t],
    B_t=[-1/t,1/t] times [-t,t]

have equal area four and form an actual compatible two-fiber family.
If a common T puts both, after arbitrary translations, inside a
fixed radius-R ball, their opposite long-axis endpoints imply
|T e_1|,|T e_2|<=R/t. Therefore |det T|<=R^2/t^2 and every transformed
area tends to zero. This confirms that the note's connected
hypothesis is essential to its stated general-d sufficiency.

## 2. Scale normalization and centroid-position control

After normalizing one anchor to contain the unit ball and lie in
the stated dimension-dependent ball, the lower relative-weight
bound eta gives positive lower and finite upper bounds for every
other fiber volume: the ratio of any two weights lies in
[eta,1/eta]. The connected finite incidence propagation applies
to diameters after this ONE common map. It does not claim that the
untranslated positions are already bounded.

For every row of the anchored relation matrix, both the target
centroid and the convex combination of source centroids are points
of the target body. Their distance is at most its diameter. The
Frobenius bound ||Ac||<=sqrt(b)D and the smallest nonzero singular
value of A give the displayed distance to ker A=L(P). This uses
membership of an average of centroids, not an identity for the
centroid of a Minkowski sum. When L(P)=Aff(P), subtracting that
projected array is exactly one ordinary base-affine shear. The
case A=0 has zero distance and is handled separately.

## 3. Anisotropic maps cannot hide the nonaffine drift

If g is nonaffine, orthogonal separation from the affine evaluation
space gives an affine dependence a with a.g nonzero. The test family
t g(z)e_1+B has uniform weights 1/|P|, so it belongs to the tested
class because eta<=1/|P|. Since g preserves every anchored relation,
all compatibility inclusions are equalities. Lattice-convexity of P
then gives exact actual integer fibers.

For arbitrary variable common T_t, the containing ball bounds the
largest singular value by R, using opposite points of each translated
ellipsoid. Positive transformed volume bounds |det T_t| below, hence
bounds the least singular value below by v/(kappa_d R^(d-1)). The
affine dependence cancels BOTH the shear and the translation, leaving
t(a.g)T_t e_1. This cannot remain bounded. The proof therefore does
cover arbitrary rotations, anisotropies, and determinants; it does
not rely on an unstated determinant-one restriction. For d=1 the
same formula has R^0 and remains valid.

## 4. Exact arithmetic graph, ranks, and convexity-space preservation

The finite anchored-representation polytopes are rational. Their
vertex relations give a rational matrix with kernel L(P), so a
rational basis extending 1,z_1,...,z_k exists. Clearing each added
basis function's denominators preserves real independence and makes
Phi(P) integral. The affine rank is exactly dim L(P)-1, by the rank
of the augmented evaluation matrix.

Every point in conv Phi(P) whose first k coordinates are integers
projects to a point z in P. The corresponding convex representation
of z is anchored, so every g_i fixes all its added coordinates.
Thus that point is Phi(z). This proves the stronger stated fiber
uniqueness, and in particular exact lattice-convexity in the FULL
standard lattice of the increased dimension. No primitive-lattice
or unit-index assumption on the graph's difference vectors is needed.

Anchored representations are preserved in both directions, so the
closure operators on the finite sets are isomorphic. Every convex
trace on a finite set is a closed trace and is realized by the
convex hull of that trace. It follows that the ordinary finite
Helly numbers agree exactly. This argument does not turn the ambient
dimension-based Doignon bound in the increased space into a sharp
continuous-fiber bound depending only on h(P).

## 5. Actual lifted fibers, measures, and the dimension cost

The graph is full rank, and a residual fiber has positive full
d-volume. Their convex hull is therefore a full convex body in
R^(ell-1) times R^d. Every integer fiber is exactly the prescribed
residual body: all integer bases are graph points and every convex
representation there projects to an original compatible one.

The map adding H(Phi(z)) is a translation on each individual fiber
and is injective on the finite mixed support, even though the ambient
map need not be injective. It preserves the mixed fiber-volume
measure and pulls original caps back to caps or to the whole source.
The pointwise depth inequality has the correct direction. Neither
the integer rank nor ambient unimodularity is claimed to survive.

Finally, an affine hull of dimension D has only D+1 independent
affine scalar functions. Making ALL ell functions in L(P) affine
requires D>=ell-1. In the archived connected example ell=5 and k=3,
so the exact graph lift uses integer rank four. The note correctly
retains the factor difference Gamma_d/16 versus Gamma_d/8 and does
not erase it merely because h is preserved.

## 6. What the verifier certifies

The verifier independently checks all 13 original integer points,
their anchored minimal faces, the connected incidence graph, the
rank-five Jensen space, the rank-four affine space, and the displayed
nonaffine dependence. The graph's rank is five after adjoining the
constant coordinate. Its integer-hull enumeration uses exact rational
barycentric coordinates in all affine bases of five lifted original
vertices. Lower-dimensional faces are covered because their affine
independent supports extend to such bases with zero extra coefficients.

The first three coordinates of every integer graph-hull point must
lie in the enumerated P, and its final coordinate lies between zero
and six, so the enumeration covers every possible integer point.
The result is exactly Phi(P). The connected 13-point obstruction is
correctly identified as an archived example; the variable-determinant
criterion and the integral-lattice realization are the refinements
being audited here.
